main_chase_cards.name: Jynx
main_chase_cards.why: Jynx is the chase because this route makes the strangest thing about the card legible: Himeno is not just drawing a Pokemon, she is using manga to explain how a card scene came to be. The open-book symbol is practically the whole thesis in miniature.

claims.text: The local row and Bulbapedia place the How I Became a Pokemon Card Vol. 3 Jynx insert on January 22, 2000; Bulbapedia's volume list gives ISBN 4889917470 for volume 3.
Bulbapedia identifies volume 3 as the third of six How I Became a Pokemon Card manga volumes created by Kagemaru Himeno and states that its included promo card is Jynx.
Bulbapedia lists the first edition as a Japanese Kadokawa-Media Factory publication dated January 22, 2000 with ISBN 4889917470.
The local source slice models one source-pinned card row for this route: Jynx source index 157.
Bulbapedia describes How I Became a Pokemon Card as a manga where each standalone story expands on the image shown on an actual Pokemon card, explaining what the Pokemon is doing or how it got there.
Bulbapedia's volume 3 page lists chapters PW15-PW21, including Twilight Jynx; this supports treating the promo as part of a story apparatus rather than a loose character promo.
Bulbapedia's Jynx card page credits both the earlier Expansion Sheet 2 print and the How I Became a Pokemon Card unnumbered promotional print to Kagemaru Himeno / 姫野かげまる.

Bulbapedia's Himeno page identifies her as an illustrator for the TCG and creator of How I Became a Pokemon Card, plus related Pokemon manga/book work including Pokemon Tales, Pokemon Card GB The Comix, and Himemaru: Pokemon Card Explorer.

Bulbapedia's Jynx card page says the How I Became a Pokemon Card unnumbered promotional print has different artwork from the Expansion Sheet 2 glossy / Quick Starter non-glossy lineage, uses a color graphic of an open book with a trading card in place of an expansion symbol, and is commonly known as Singing Jynx or Natta Wake Jynx.

Agents should keep this Vol. 3 Jynx route separate from CoroCoro April 1998 Jynx, Expansion Sheet 2 glossy Jynx, Quick Starter Gift Set non-glossy Jynx, Base/Expansion Pack Jynx, later Jynx-line Smoochum listings, and the other How I Became a Pokemon Card volume inserts.

The catalog can make the Vol. 3 book route, open-book symbol, nickname context, and Jynx row identity legible, but it does not prove seller possession, authenticity, condition, price, complete book/insert state, or spendability.

narrative.human_title: How I Became a Pokemon Card Vol. 3 — the card explains itself
narrative.why_it_matters: This manga lane is one of the project’s clearest examples of assembly history. The card is not merely bundled with a book; the book is a machine for making the card image make sense. Volume 3 gives that apparatus to Jynx: chapter list, promo insert, Himeno authorship, and a symbol that is literally an open book with a card inside it. For an agent, that is the whole clue. The right match is not just a Jynx. It is Jynx as a story-object from Pokemon Card ni Natta Wake.

special_identification_instructions.summary: Treat Vol. 3 Jynx as a manga/book insert route with a specific open-book symbol and Himeno story apparatus, not as a generic Jynx or generic Natta Wake listing.

Expect the card to be connected to the Vol. 3 manga insert, not merely to a loose Jynx character listing.
Look for the color open-book-with-trading-card symbol context; this is a key route tell for the How I Became a Pokemon Card promo print.
Use Kagemaru Himeno / 姫野かげまる as the expected author/illustrator lane, while remembering that catalog credit is not physical-card proof.
Separate this row from CoroCoro April 1998 Jynx row 039, Expansion Sheet 2 glossy Jynx, Quick Starter non-glossy Jynx, Base/Expansion Pack Jynx, and later Smoochum/Jynx-line listings.
Separate Vol. 3 Jynx from Vol. 1 Mankey, Vol. 2 Psyduck, Vol. 4 Sunkern, Vol. 5 Hoppip, and Vol. 6 _____'s Pikachu.

card_highlights.why_it_matters: Jynx is already a route-sensitive Pokemon, and this print makes that sensitivity useful. The Vol. 3 card is not just another Jynx image; it is a Himeno story-card, nicknamed Singing Jynx, carrying the open-book mark of a manga that asks why the card picture exists.

narrative.human_title: Jynx — Singing Jynx, Natta Wake Jynx, the card inside the book
narrative.why_it_matters: This Jynx print is wonderfully self-aware. A manga about how Pokemon became cards includes a Jynx card whose symbol is an open book with a card inside it. That is almost too perfect for this project: the route tells you how to read the object. Keep the name, the song, the book mark, and Himeno together, and the card stops being a stray Jynx and becomes a tiny artifact of how Pokemon explained its own pictures.
